title: Scanner with Keywords, Silent Drop Bug, and Edge Cases
description: A scanner tokenizes four test inputs showing keyword recognition, the '12foo' splitting into NUMBER+NAME, and the silent drop of '@' because no pattern matches it. Three TODOs highlight design decisions.
source: draft: omp free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Imports and Token dataclass with type and value fields (no line number in this version).

scan function: patterns list with regex for NUMBER, NAME, operators, parens, SKIP. Keywords set for reserved words. Master pattern joins with named groups. finditer loop skips SKIP, classifies matched text as KEYWORD if in keywords else pattern name, appends Token.
The loop: SKIP continues silently. Keyword check happens after matching, so 'let' matches NAME pattern but becomes KEYWORD token.

steps.question: What tokens does '12foo' produce and why?
steps.answer: NUMBER(12) NAME(foo) because NUMBER pattern matches digits and NAME matches the remaining letters

steps.description: Test loop output: 'let x = 3 + 4' -> KEYWORD NAME EQ NUMBER PLUS NUMBER. 'lambda y in y * 2' -> KEYWORD NAME KEYWORD NAME STAR NUMBER. '12foo' -> NUMBER NAME; '3 @ 4' -> NUMBER NUMBER (the @ is silently dropped).
TODO comments: 12foo splits because scanner matches longest prefix for each pattern greedily; @ is silently dropped because no pattern matches it and finditer advances past it  -  this is a bug.
